title: Levels gained per promotion
prompt: The promotions board shows how many levels each promotion moved someone up. Write `solve(promotions)` so it returns the promotions table with that number added and the raise column renamed.
rules: Add `levels_gained` at the end: `to_level` minus `from_level`. A missing level gives a missing `levels_gained`.
Rename `salary_increase` to `raise_amount`, in the same position.
Keep every other column as it is, and every row, duplicates included.
hints: `withColumn` adds a column at the end and keeps all the others.
Subtract one column from another: `F.col("to_level") - F.col("from_level")`.
`withColumnRenamed("old", "new")` renames a column and leaves it where it was.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(promotions):
    # Add levels_gained and rename salary_increase to raise_amount.
    return promotions
explanation: Two small changes, chained: `promotions.withColumn("levels_gained", F.col("to_level") - F.col("from_level")).withColumnRenamed("salary_increase", "raise_amount")`. `withColumn` keeps every column and adds the new one at the end; `withColumnRenamed` keeps the renamed column in its place. The order of the two steps doesn't matter here. A missing level makes the difference missing without extra code. Most promotions move one level, so `F.lit(1)` looks right on the sample but is wrong for a promotion that skips a level.
